text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Thursday:
- A verdict to be delivered today in the case against the editor and a journalist of an independent weekly charged with criminal defamation of president Franjo Tudjman.

- Forensic experts of the U.N. war crimes tribunal have so far found remains of some 40-50 people buried in the Ovcara mass grave. They were killed after the Serbs seized the Eastern Slavonian town of Vukovar.
- A list of the best paid managers, issued by the Central Payments' Bureau (ZAP), headed by a director of a private engineering company who earned 244,961 kuna in June.
Bank and insurance firms' managers who earned 33,000 and 31,500 kuna also top the list.
- In the first eight months of 1996, state oil company INA produced 952,970 tonnes of crude and derivatives, or two percent more than planned.
- January-August exports, totalling $2.94 billion, down 1.4 percent from the same period last year.
- Support IFOR troops help the economy. The Sibenik county alone estimated to have earned 12 million German marks.
- Some 50,000 of the employed on sick leave every day.
- Ruling HDZ party proposes a new round of talks with the opposition for solving the crisis over the local power structure in Zagreb.
- Croatia is soon to have a climate like Great Britain, says Zvonimir Katusic, assistant head of the State Weather Bureau.
- Croatia Airlines to cut domestic tarrifs 20-50 percent.
- Croatia and IFOR sign a deal on the use of ports at 50 percent of the current fees. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
